criteria.text: helixa-new pulls the latest successful production Qdrant snapshot over SSH with a root-owned mode-0600 key whose forced command cannot open a shell, forward ports, or read any Qdrant credential.
A pulled generation becomes visible only after its manifest, exact 1.18.2 version, freshness, byte length, and SHA-256 all validate; incomplete or altered data remains hidden and is discarded.
The backup host runs one low-priority off-peak pull per day, refuses to run below 10 GiB free, and retains no more than 14 successful daily generations and no generation older than 14 days.

An isolated restore drill uses the same digest-pinned Qdrant 1.18.2 image, stays inside explicit CPU, memory, process, and loopback-network limits, and proves the restored point count equals the manifest.
Production Prometheus receives separate off-host backup and restore timestamps only after success; missing or stale evidence reaches the existing Telegram route at 36 hours and 35 days respectively.

The live configuration is installed reversibly, one real backup and exact-version restore drill pass, rollback is documented, and no reindex, schema migration, paid call, or production application-data mutation is performed.
